cohortGate.enforcement: The authenticated server caller verifies the allowlisted adult, English-language, US, first-marathon cohort record before invoking the pure generator. The generator must not infer these facts from identity or locale data.

consistentRunningWeeks.implementationGap: The approved value requires a new normalized input field; the current plan-generation contract does not collect consistency duration.

currentWeeklyDistanceMeters.calculation: completed running distance during the prior 28 complete days divided by 4

currentRunningFrequencyDaysPerWeek.calculation: count of distinct run days during the prior 28 complete days divided by 4

availableTrainingDays.requiredPattern: preferred long-run day plus weekdays 2, 4, and 6 days after it, modulo seven

safetySignal.enforcement: The authenticated caller may invoke this ruleset only after an approved beta-safety artifact handles every other state.

feasibility.alignment: target race date equals plan start date plus (whole weeks times 7) minus 1 day
feasibility.leadInWeeks: whole weeks from plan start to race minus 18

planFamily.name: Founding beta completion plan
planFamily.effortBoundary: All non-race running is conversational easy effort. The draft contains no pace, heart-rate, finish-time, interval, tempo, hill, or threshold prescription.

recoveryWeek.workouts: one rest assignment on each day

rules: A load week may return to a previously completed high after a cutback.
A new pre-race weekly-distance high may exceed the prior high by no more than 2000 meters.
A new pre-race long-run high may exceed the prior high by no more than 2000 meters.
Race distance is not treated as a training-load increase or used to justify a later progression.
The generator never adds intensity, a fifth training run, or distance beyond the frozen table.

unsupportedEvaluation.rule: If any reason applies, return unsupported with all applicable reason codes in this order and no generated plan.

sources.observed: An 18-week conservative plan intended for runners averaging four to five running days per week with a longest run around 40 minutes; it uses conversational regular and long running and reaches a 165-minute long run.
sources.use: Supports reviewing an 18-week, four-day-or-more completion-oriented family; it does not validate Marathoner's numeric eligibility thresholds.

sources.observed: The B.A.A. novice plan averages four running days, begins near 25 miles per week, peaks near 40 miles per week, and uses 16-to-18-mile long runs.
sources.use: Informs review of the proposed starting volume, frequency, peak volume, and 28-kilometer peak long run without copying the B.A.A. schedule.

sources.observed: Among 441 marathon runners, less than 40 kilometers per week and a longest run below 25 kilometers were associated with slower finish times; measured training variables were not associated with new running-related injuries in this cohort.
sources.use: Supports scrutiny of training sufficiency and a long run above 25 kilometers, but does not establish a safety threshold or causal prescription.

sources.observed: Among 735 New York City Marathon entrants, training injury incidence was 40 percent and more days at an acute-to-chronic distance ratio of at least 1.5 were associated with injury.
sources.use: Supports avoiding large training-load spikes; it does not validate one universal week-to-week cap.

sources.observed: Novice runners increasing distance by more than 30 percent over two weeks appeared more vulnerable to distance-related injury than runners increasing by less than 10 percent.
sources.use: Supports reviewer scrutiny of progression spikes; the population and exploratory design do not validate Marathoner's exact increments.

sources.observed: A novice-runner program applying the 10-percent rule did not reduce running-related injury versus a shorter standard program.
sources.use: Prevents representing a 10-percent rule as proven injury prevention. Marathoner's two-kilometer increments remain a product proposal requiring review.

sources.observed: In more than 158,000 recreational marathon training histories, disciplined tapers up to three weeks were associated with better performance than shorter or less disciplined tapers.
sources.use: Informs the proposed three-week progressive taper; it does not prove the exact distances are optimal for this beta segment.
